title: The Electron Beam, from Tip to Measurement: the hand-over contract
written: 2026-11-09, scaffold session S1, from PLAN.md section 6
rules: Every stored value is in coherent SI units: m, s, kg, A, K, mol, and derived units (V, T, J, Pa, sr). No eV, nm, mbar or degrees Celsius inside a value.

A symbol may carry a display unit (display_unit) and the factor that turns the SI value into it (display_scale): shown = value * display_scale. Energies are stored in J and shown in eV; the eV is accepted for use with the SI, it is never stored.
Each symbol has one meaning on the whole page. Its key is the name used in physics/chNN.js, ref/chNN.py and text/chNN.py.
A stage reads only the symbols listed under its 'in' and the 'out' of earlier stages, and writes only its 'out'.
A chapter that needs a new symbol or a change here writes the request in notes/electron-beam/requests.md; the scaffold or the coordinator edits this file.

types.number: a finite IEEE 754 double in the SI unit given
types.integer: a whole number stored as a double
types.enum: one of the strings listed in 'values'
types.material: an object {Z, A, rho, J, name}: atomic number, molar mass in kg/mol, density in kg/m^3, mean ionisation energy in J
types.profile: an object {kind, pitch, cd, height, sidewall}: kind 'line-space' or 'fin'; lengths in m; sidewall angle in rad
types.array: a list of numbers (a curve or a trajectory); its unit is the symbol's unit

lambda_opt.meaning: wavelength of the light in an optical inspection tool

NA.meaning: numerical aperture of the optical objective

w_feat.meaning: width of the smallest feature on the wafer that must be seen

d_opt.meaning: smallest period (pitch) light can resolve, Abbe limit lambda_opt/(2 NA); the half-pitch is half of it

ratio_opt.meaning: Abbe period over feature width; for equal lines and spaces (pitch 2w) light cannot resolve the pattern when this exceeds 2

E_field.meaning: uniform electric field, its y component (the tube of section 1.3 has E = (0, -E, 0), so its slider value is the negative of E there)

B_field.meaning: uniform magnetic flux density, its z component (section 1.3 uses B = (0, 0, -B_p))

theta_0.meaning: angle of the initial velocity to the magnetic field

energy_drift.meaning: relative change of kinetic energy over the run, (E_end - E_start)/E_start

trajectory.meaning: positions x, y, z of the electron at each stored step

t_run.meaning: duration of the run: the time over which the electron is followed in the uniform fields (the plate transit time in Thomson's tube)
t_run.note: the module enlarges dt, if it must, so that a run has at most 400 000 steps

x_end.meaning: x position of the electron at the end of the run

y_end.meaning: y position of the electron at the end of the run

z_end.meaning: z position of the electron at the end of the run (along B)

theta_end.meaning: angle of the velocity at the end of the run to the +x axis, measured in the x-y plane: the deflection angle when the field region ends

r_t.meaning: radius of the emitter tip apex

V_ex.meaning: extraction voltage between tip and extractor

phi.meaning: work function of the emitter surface
phi.note: default 4.5 eV, polycrystalline tungsten as in chapter 2 (which states its source); finisher, 9 November 2026

p.meaning: residual gas pressure at the tip

t_clean.meaning: time since the last cleaning flash of the tip

k_f.meaning: field factor in F = V_ex/(k_f r_t)

I_e.meaning: total emission current from the tip

B_r.note: axial differential reduced brightness (chapter 3); default: chapter 2 at its defaults

dE.meaning: full width at half maximum of the energy distribution of emitted electrons
dE.note: default: chapter 2 at its defaults (0.215 eV)

dE50.meaning: FW50 of the energy distribution of emitted electrons: the narrowest energy interval that holds half of them
dE50.note: default: chapter 2 at its defaults (0.157 eV); used by the FW50 chromatic term of chapter 5 (Bronsgeest et al. 2008, Eq. 20)

theta_cov.meaning: fraction of the tip surface covered by adsorbed gas

V_land.meaning: landing voltage: the energy per charge with which electrons hit the wafer (after any retarding field)

E_0.meaning: kinetic energy of the beam electrons, e V_acc

lambda_e.meaning: relativistic de Broglie wavelength of the beam electrons

V_star.meaning: relativistically corrected voltage V (1 + eV/(2 m c^2))

V_star_land.meaning: relativistically corrected landing voltage V_land (1 + e V_land/(2 m c^2))

lambda_land.meaning: de Broglie wavelength of the electrons when they land on the wafer

ang_mag.meaning: factor by which a paraxial beam angle grows when the beam is decelerated from V_acc to V_land: sqrt(V*_acc / V*_land)

lambda_curve.meaning: the wavelength against voltage for the figure: pairs (V, lambda relativistic, lambda non-relativistic) on 61 log-spaced voltages from 10 V to 1 MV, flattened

NI.meaning: lens excitation: coil turns times current
NI.note: ampere-turns; the turn count is dimensionless

a_lens.meaning: half-width at half maximum of the bell-shaped lens field

u_obj.meaning: object distance: from the object plane (source or intermediate image) to the lens centre

WD.meaning: working distance: from the objective lens centre to the wafer

B_0.meaning: peak axial flux density of the lens, from NI and a: B_0 = mu_0 NI/(2a) for the Glaser field

M.meaning: lateral magnification of the column (image size over object size)

C_s.meaning: spherical aberration coefficient referred to the image side
C_s.note: default: chapter 4's objective at its defaults

C_c.meaning: chromatic aberration coefficient referred to the image side
C_c.note: default: chapter 4's objective at its defaults

theta_rot.meaning: image rotation by the magnetic lens (Larmor angle)

omega_G.meaning: Glaser's lens parameter omega = sqrt(1 + k^2), k^2 = e B_0^2 a^2 / (8 m V*): how strong the lens is (1 = no lens, 2 = the ray crosses the axis twice inside the field)

lens_ray.meaning: the axial paraxial ray from the object to the wafer for the figure: pairs (z, r) for unit slope at the object, flattened

alpha.meaning: beam half-angle at the wafer, set by the aperture

d_p.meaning: probe diameter at the wafer (FW50 unless the classic sum is chosen in chapter 5)
d_p.note: default: chapter 5 at its defaults (5.32 nm FW50)

probe_convention.meaning: how the probe diameter is defined: fw50, the diameter holding half the current (root-power sum, Barth and Kruit 1996; coefficients of Bronsgeest et al. 2008), or rss, the classic quadrature sum

d_I.meaning: diameter of the source image at the wafer that carries the asked probe current at the angle alpha (Bronsgeest et al. 2008, Eq. 6)

d_A.meaning: diffraction contribution to the probe diameter, in the chosen convention

d_S.meaning: spherical-aberration contribution to the probe diameter, in the chosen convention

d_C.meaning: chromatic-aberration contribution to the probe diameter, in the chosen convention

d_p_opt.meaning: the smallest probe diameter for the asked current, at alpha_opt

spot_curve.meaning: for the figure: (alpha, d_A, d_S, d_C, d_I, d_p) on 61 log-spaced angles from 0.1 to 100 mrad, flattened

E_land.meaning: landing energy of the beam electrons on the wafer, e V_land

material.meaning: target material: Si, Al, Cu or Au (the elements for which chapter 6 has both backscattering data and secondary-electron constants)
material.note: finisher: an enum with the material table inside physics/ch06.js (Z, molar mass, ESTAR density, Lin and Joy eps and lambda_s); J from Joy 1991 Eq. 12

delta_SE.meaning: secondary electron yield (secondary electrons out per primary in)

R.meaning: electron range in the target (Kanaya-Okayama unless stated)

V_int.meaning: volume of the interaction region, taken as the hemisphere of radius r90 about the point of impact

sigma_sig.meaning: lateral spread (standard deviation) of the escaping signal around the beam axis

sig_core.meaning: width of the core of the escaping secondary signal (the median of |x| divided by 0.67449, the value for a Gaussian)

f_core.meaning: fraction of the escaping secondary signal within three core widths of the beam

sig_halo.meaning: root-mean-square width of the rest of the escaping secondary signal (the halo made by backscattered electrons)

u_eta.meaning: statistical standard error of eta_BSE from the finite number of simulated electrons

u_delta.meaning: statistical standard error of delta_SE from the finite number of simulated electrons

r90.meaning: radius about the point of impact of the hemisphere that holds 90 % of the energy left in the wafer

mc_paths.meaning: for the figure: the first 40 trajectories, each as (number of points n, 1 if backscattered else 0, x1, z1, ..., xn, zn) in nm, concatenated

N_px.meaning: pixels per scan line and scan lines per image (a square image); the lines along the feature are averaged into one profile

eta_c.meaning: fraction of the emitted signal electrons that the detector collects
eta_c.note: Applied Materials' public product page quotes 95 % for its back-scatter detector; that is quoted as a public claim only, never as a model input

cd.meaning: true critical dimension: the width of the line at half its height

t_ov.meaning: time per measurement site besides the scan: stage move, focus, pattern recognition (an assumed value, not a vendor number)

SNR.meaning: signal-to-noise ratio of the edge contrast

sigma_CD.meaning: standard deviation of the measured critical dimension

tol_rt.meaning: spread of the tip radius (relative standard deviation), for the tolerance Monte Carlo; an assumed value

tol_NI.meaning: drift of the objective excitation (relative standard deviation), for the tolerance Monte Carlo; an assumed value

tol_p.meaning: spread of the gun pressure (standard deviation of its natural logarithm), for the tolerance Monte Carlo; an assumed value

tol_z.meaning: wafer height error left after focusing (standard deviation), for the tolerance Monte Carlo; an assumed value

spec_cd.meaning: precision required of a width measurement (largest acceptable sigma_CD); an assumed value

dose_max.meaning: largest acceptable dose per image; an assumed value

I_beam.meaning: probe current with the condensers left at their nominal setting (it moves when the source changes)

sens.meaning: normalised sensitivities (x/y) dy/dx of d_p, I_beam, sigma_CD and MPH (rows) to r_t, V_ex, p, V_land, I_p, WD, a_lens, t_d, N_px, eta_c (columns), by central differences of +-1 % in x, flattened by rows

pwin.meaning: for the figure: sigma_CD on a 14 x 14 grid of landing voltage (0.5 to 5 kV) and probe current (1 pA to 1 nA), both logarithmic, each point with the best aperture, flattened by voltage

tol_dp_sd.meaning: standard deviation of the probe diameter over the tolerance Monte Carlo

tol_cd_p95.meaning: 95th percentile of sigma_CD over the tolerance Monte Carlo

tol_yield.meaning: fraction of the tolerance Monte Carlo samples that meet the precision spec_cd

CD_meas.meaning: the CD the edge algorithm reads from the noise-free profile (its offset from cd is the bias of the method)

sigma_CD_mc.meaning: standard deviation of the measured CD from repeating the noisy measurement (Monte Carlo, 1000 repeats)

dose.meaning: charge per area that one scan of the image puts on the wafer

n_pe.meaning: mean number of beam electrons per pixel

prof_curve.meaning: for the figure: per pixel across one period (x, mean counts of one line, counts of one noisy line, mean of the N_px noisy lines), flattened
